name: Exp A: Practical tirzepatide long-forms (Lane A)
hypothesis: Long-tail practical tirzepatide questions that people search for beat approved-drug deep dives and keep gaining views over time.
change: Lane A on every day without qualifying news, with the long-tail searched question first in the title.
metric: Success: day-7 median of 25+ views and 60+ watch minutes, still growing at day 28.
result: Won at n=8+. It earns 71% of tracked long-form minutes, and the big three have 564–634 min each. Caveat from this week: the 7 Lane A videos since 10-27 have a median of only about 41 min (0–137) at 3–9 days old. The last 4 shipped with scenes out of sync, so this looks like a production failure, not proof the lane is weakening. Lane A stays the default, with the beat-sync check as a ship-blocker.

name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane would also work as long-form.
change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B.
result: Closed early at n=1. The pharmacy check got 19 views and 61 min. Gray-market stays Shorts-only, at most 1 a week.

name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a new named result
hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a newly public named trial result drives more long-form views than evergreen topics.
change: The long-form slot went to qualifying fresh randomized results.
result: Retired at n=1 (petrelintide: 37 views, 160 min). Looking back at fresh next-gen results, the median is about 35 views. News goes to 13:00 Shorts. Only a randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide may get an extra L2.

name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified description link
hypothesis: A 20:00 Short that asks a fresh question a live long-form answers, with a verified description link, lifts that long-form's daily views.
change: The 20:00 Short pointed to a live Lane A long-form, with 'link in the description'.
metric: The target long-form's views in the 3 days after the Short vs the 3 days before, plus its SHORTS traffic.
min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link
result: Closed with no valid data point. The way it was meant to work can't work: YouTube made links in Shorts descriptions and comments unclickable on 31 Aug 2023. That explains why SHORTS traffic is 0 on all 23 long-forms with traffic data. Replaced by Exp G, which uses the Studio related-video link, the only clickable link in the Shorts player.

name: Exp E: State-change thumbnail (What to Eat, plus Strength as a second test)
hypothesis: Our two most-shown practical videos have a packaging problem, not a discovery problem. A state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer lifts CTR toward the 3.8–4.7% that Side Effects, How Long and Protein get.
change: Only the thumbnail changes, no body imagery. What to Eat was swapped on about 11-04 (publisher must confirm the time). Strength is swapped on 11-10 as a second test of the same change. No other edits to either video for 14 days.
metric: CTR on impressions after the swap vs CTR just before it, judged per video and with views per day not falling. Before-swap baselines: What to Eat about 1.9% on 568 impressions (11-02→11-05), 2.53% overall; Strength about 0.6% on 467 impressions, 2.10% overall. Success: new-impression CTR of 3.0%+ on both.
min_sample: 1,000 new impressions or 14 days per video, whichever comes later (What to Eat around 11-18, Strength around 11-24)
result: Not readable yet, and the analytics feed is stuck at 11-05. Watch-out: CTR naturally falls as impressions spread to more surfaces, so compare against the before-swap rate, not the overall average.

name: Exp F: A benefit-framed subscribe line in Shorts
hypothesis: One honest line that names the channel's promise will at least double Shorts subscriber conversion (about 0.5–0.6 per 1,000 views).
change: On 08:00 and 13:00 Shorts only, the second-to-last line is 'We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps.' 20:00 Shorts get no line and act as the control.
metric: subscribersGained per 1,000 views at day 7, line vs control. Also channel subscribers per day vs the 1.3-a-day baseline. Success: 2× the control rate and 2.5+ channel subscribers a day.
min_sample: 14 days (11-03 to 11-17), about 28 Shorts with the line and 14 without
result: Early channel-level read is weak: +0 subscribers since 11-04 (5 days) vs a 1.3-a-day baseline. That's confounded by Shorts views falling to about 130 a day (from about 300), two missed days, and the line missing on 2 Shorts on 11-06. Per-Short day-7 data starts 11-11. If the channel is still under 1 subscriber a day at day 14, close it as lost.

name: Exp G: Studio related-video link on top Shorts
hypothesis: The related-video link is the only clickable path from a Short. Setting it on our highest-view body-worry Shorts will create SHORTS traffic to Lane A long-forms. Those viewers watch at long-form rates and subscribe about 5× more often than Shorts viewers.
change:
The owner sets one related-video link on each of these Shorts:
- hair grow-back (1,019 views) → the Hair long-form once it's verified clean, Side Effects until then
- bones (242) → Bones & Muscle
- injection site (226) → Side Effects
- nausea (166) → Side Effects
- muscle (136) → Strength
- breakfast (111) → What to Eat
- constipation fibre (92) → Constipation
- Thanksgiving Short (11-06) → Thanksgiving
No other change to those Shorts.
metric: SHORTS-source views and minutes on each target long-form in the 7 days after the link vs 0 before. Success: at least 1 long-form view per 100 new Short views across the set, plus a visible rise in channel subscribers.
min_sample: 8 linked Shorts, 7 days after the link is set
result: Waiting on the owner. It starts the day the links are set. It needs advanced features turned on in Studio.
